Vide this Judgment, I shall dispose of the petition filed by the petitioners for grant of compensation u/s 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'M.V. Act') for the fatal injuries suffered by Sh. Sangram Singh in the road accident.
Initially, the petition / application was filed u/s 166 and 140 of the M.V. Act.

However, subsequently, an application was filed on behalf of petitioners seeking conversion of the claim petition from Section 166 & 140 M.V. Act to Section 164 M.V. Act and the same was allowed vide order dated 06.01.2023 passed by Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal.

2. Briefly, the case of the petitioners is that on 27.03.2013 at about 3.30 to 4 pm, Sh. Sangram Singh (hereinafter referred to as 'deceased') alongwith Sh. Pawan Kumar were going to Tigari, District Gautam Budh Nagar from Khoda Colony by motorcycle bearing registration no. DL8SAY- 5469 (Pulsar), which was driven by Pawan Kumar at a normal speed and on the correct side of the road and when the motorcycle reached at NH-24, Akbarpur, Behrampur, PS Vijay Nagar, Ghaziabad, a three wheeler (passenger) bearing registration no. UP14CT-9222 (hereinafter referred to as Digitally signed SACHIN by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.10.08 MACT No. 76917/16 Date of Award 08.10.2024 17:18:03 +0530

Page No. 2 of 15 'offending vehicle'), being driven by its driver / respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner hit against the motorcycle with great force, as a result of which, the motorcycle fell down on the road and Sh.
Sangram Singh received fatal injuries, who died at the spot.

It is further stated that he was taken to District Hospital, Ghaziabad, where his postmortem was conducted vide No. 435/13 dated 28.03.2023.
3.
As per the claim petition, the respondent no.1 is the driver as well as owner of the offending vehicle and respondent no. 2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
It is further stated that deceased was aged about 28 years at the time of accident, who left behind his legal heirs namely Smt. Kiran Devi (wife of deceased) and two children namely Siva and Omji.

4. Respondent no. 1 Brijesh Kumar was served by way of publication in Daily Newspaper 'Vir Arjun'
and since, none has appeared on behalf of the respondent no.1, he was proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 23.05.2018 passed by the Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal.
5.
A reply was filed on behalf of the respondent no.2, wherein it is stated inter alia

that the answering respondent is not liable to pay any compensation as it was the driver of the pulsar motorcycle bearing no. 6. From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 23.05.2018:-

1 . Whether Sangram Singh suffered fatal injuries in a vehicular accident that took place on 27.03.2013 at about 3.30 to 4 pm at NH-24, Akbarpur, Behrampur, PS Vijay Nagar, Ghaziabad involving a vehicle bearing registration no. UP14CT 9222, owned and driven by respondent no.1 Brijesh Kumar and insured with Respondent Shri Ram General Insurance Company Limited?
OPP 2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP 3. Relief.
7.

PW1 is Smt.

He denied that the present letter was gathered or collected from Brijesh Kumar unlawfully after completion of investigation or that the said letter was given by Brijesh Kumar under his pressure and to help out the petitioners.
He denied that he had not conducted a fair enquiry/investigation in the present FIR and protected the driver/owner of the vehicle bearing no. UP14CT-1537.
He denied that he had falsely implicated the driver of vehicle bearing no. UP14CT-9222 or that he was deposing falsely.

16.
Admittedly, PW1 Smt. Kiran Devi was not present at the spot at the time of accident and she had not witnessed the accident.

However, in support of their case, petitioners also got examined IO/Inspector Ramashray Singh as PW-2, who has deposed that he investigated the matter and filed chargesheet against the driver Brijesh Kumar, who was driving the vehicle bearing registration No.
UP14CT-9222 on the date of accident.

It is evident from his testimony that, initially, the vehicle bearing no. UP14CT-1537 was mentioned as an offending vehicle in the FIR, however, later on, in his investigation, it was revealed that the vehicle bearing no. UP14CT-9222 was the offending vehicle.

It is further evident from the testimony of the IO / PW-2 that the correct offending vehicle i.e. UP14CT-9222 was revealed on the statement of Mr. Pawan, who has given the affidavit, which is part of Ex.PW2/A at page no. 9 and 10, who was also an injured in the present case.

It is also transpired from the testimony of IO / PW-2 that he had enquired from the owner of the vehicle bearing no. 14, which is part of Ex.PW2/A. IO / PW2 has filed the copy of inner case diary in respect of his investigation in the present FIR, which is Ex.PW2/A (Colly).

Issue No.2 21.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation.
The petitioners are seeking compensation under Section 164 M.V. Act.
As per Section 164 M.V. Act, the compensation payable in case of death shall be Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs).
In view of the same, the petitioners are held entitled to the compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lacs only).
LIABILITY 22.
Now the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.

Since, indisputably, the aforesaid vehicle bearing no. UP 14 CT9222 (offending vehicle) was duly insured with the respondent No. 2 / Insurance Company, therefore, respondent No. 2 / Insurance Co. is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners / claimants.
Issue no. 2 is decided accordingly.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Issue no. 1 is decided accordingly.
Issue No.2 21.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation.
The petitioners are seeking compensation under Section 164 M.V. Act.
As per Section 164 M.V. Act, the compensation payable in case of death shall be Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs).
In view of the same, the petitioners are held entitled to the compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lacs only).
LIABILITY 22.
Now the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Since, indisputably, the aforesaid vehicle bearing no. UP 14 CT9222 (offending vehicle) was duly insured with the respondent No. 2 / Insurance Company, therefore, respondent No. 2 / Insurance Co. is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners / claimants.
Issue no. 2 is decided accordingly.
